template_notes.text: The ESS settings are stored in the GX's flash and kept when the gateway stops. A rule that commands them must move in steps; the template spaces writes a minute apart. The commands carry no release value: a released rule leaves the setting as it is unless the device's command binding sets `safe` (a release value depends on the site).
The grid setpoint is followed in ESS modes 1 and 2; in mode 3 (external control) the GX ignores it, so the command refuses to write.

Read 0 on a DVM-S with an HE hydro kit (field-checked 2026-10-08), with the compressor running: water flow, pump PWM, room sensor, heater-out and tank temperatures, water-out target, DC link voltage, outdoor fan speed, EVA-in temperature (0x82DE is 'Eva In for EHS') and the experimental energy rows. Why: the HE kit has no flow sensor and switches its water pump on/off (DVM HT/HE installation manual DB68-03973A-06); and these NASA IDs are not in Samsung's list for HE/HT/EHS (MIM manual DB68-07538A-03, Table 3, which names only 0x4087, 0x42F1 and 0x4067) — they come from the community, tested on an EHS system. Each row's description says whether its ID is official or community. On an HE kit, leave these unselected rather than trust a 0; an EHS unit may fill them.

Quiet mode and the compressor limit (FR control, NASA 0x42F1) have no effect on an HE hydro kit: the write is accepted and nothing changes. Samsung documents FR control for hydro units with an integrated tank only.

The values at 4-28 and 82-96 appear only after the setup steps are written (at connect, with writes allowed on the device). A defrost (outdoor_defrost On, step 1-30) after a hard start in cold, humid air is normal.

Heat output is ESTIMATED from the water ΔT and an assumed constant flow, water_flow_assumed (l/min): set it to your circuit's measured flow in the device's Calculated tab (its expression is a plain number). Not the pump's maximum, not Samsung's minimum — an HE kit has no flow sensor and an on/off pump, so the flow is roughly constant while it runs. COP = heat output / electric power, taken from the meter named in Device → Edit → Electricity measured by (power_electric) when there is one, else estimated from the compressor current: √3 × 400 V × I × 0.95 (power_electric_estimated; edit the voltage or the power factor in its expression). The estimate leaves out the fans and the water pump. A heat meter and an electricity meter give the exact COP.

Before any command: wire an emergency stop that cuts the drive's supply, keep the keypad STOP key active (Pr 02.01) and set Pr 09.02 = 1 with Pr 09.03 = 2.0 s, so the motor ramps to a stop by itself if the gateway, the bus or the cable goes away. MBG polls every 2 s, which keeps that time-out fed.
Runtime control writes only 2000H-2002H. Do not write the drive's parameters (GGnnH) from rules or loops: parameters are stored in the drive's memory, and repeated writes wear it out.

Version 0.1.0 is written from the manual and not yet checked on a drive. If the drive answers a block read of 2100H-210AH (the manual allows up to 20 words for status), Max registers per read can go up to 20 for fewer requests, provided the parameter rows (0200H, 0201H, 0902H, 0903H) stay unselected, since a parameter is read one per request.
set_frequency refuses to write unless Pr 02.00 = 3 (frequency from RS-485): otherwise the drive would ignore it silently.
